_about: Frame and spec checks from the Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026 failure lists (docs/learning/2026-11-19-frame-checks.md; scripts/velib/qc_frames.py). Each block is one check: its numbers, and the words Krish said that it enforces. Every number here is a first value taken from those two pieces and is Krish's to change; no code holds a threshold. A check reads props and, where it says so, the rendered frames; a frame check that cannot read its frames (no tesseract, no face detector) reports not_run and is never a pass. HOW TO ADD A ROW FOR THE NEXT FAULT: (1) add a block here with 'enforces' (his exact words), 'binds_from' if it differs, and its numbers; (2) write one pure function in qc_frames.py that returns a list of problems and add it to SPEC_ROWS (props only) or FRAME_ROWS (needs the render); (3) add a good case and a bad case to tests/ve_frame_checks_test.py; (4) add its failure to config/failures.json naming the test as its guard. Never add a threshold in code.
binds_from_why: The Tue 17 piece is the earliest one in production that met these faults, and neither it nor Wed 18 has shipped. A piece published before this date is measured and shown advisory, never counted (config/failures.json F33).

one_carrier.enforces: "two concurrent visual styles trying to say the same thing over one another? why?" (Krish, Tue 17): one picture per beat; a graphic and a photo never both carry the same point.

backdrop.enforces: "Motion graphics on a flat black background, straight after a full-frame photograph" (Krish, Tue 17): a graphics beat sits on a graded backdrop, never on black.

figures.enforces: Tue 17 items 2 and 9: a figure (kinetic_stat, stat_strip) is never dimmed or blurred, and the figure a beat exists to show fills the frame.

ghost_face.enforces: "A ghost of his face in dissolves" (Krish, Tue 17): a change between a full-screen beat and a face beat is a clean cut.

render_current.enforces: "NO ICONS, ONLY THE WORDMARK DURING THE TITLE FRAME AND THE CLOSING FRAME" (Krish, 18 Nov): a cut whose props do not say bodyLogo, or say true when the palette says false, was rendered before the rule and is refused.

off_day_text.enforces: "off.day is NEVER to be used ever as a tag" (Krish, 18 Nov): the string is drawn nowhere, in any cut.

title.enforces: Tue 17 items 6 and 8 and Wed 18 item 5: captions are empty for the whole title hold; the title is built from his spoken line and timed to his words; it arrives as a card (title_moment.card), never bare words over his face, at full stage width.

title_lockup.enforces: "I expect the title card to enter as I am talking, and the title of the piece is woven in to my script at the start. This is a good example of what actually was a good build for the title card" (Krish, 19 Nov 2026, of Wed 11's "AI MUSIC or HUMAN MUSIC?" after Wed 18's title came out squeezed into his panel with the wordmark as a separate layer): the title is ONE full-frame lockup, centred, with the wordmark inside it, entering and leaving with it.
title_lockup.min_cap_height_why: Measured on the frame by tesseract, whose box for a capital word is its cap height, about 0.73 of Anton's font size. Wed 11's good build set 184 px type on a 1920 px tall frame (cap height about 7% of the frame) and 194 px on a 1080 px wide one (about 13%); Wed 18's failed card set about 70 px on 1920 (about 2.7%). The floors sit between: 4% tall (about 105 px type) and 6.5% wide (about 96 px type), so a squeezed card fails and a two-line long title still passes.
title_lockup.min_width_why: A lockup's bands span 92% of the frame; read words fill most of a band. A title confined to his 608 px panel on a 1920 px wide cut spans at most 32%, and to Wed 18's 800 px box on a tall cut at most 74% of 1080 at full stretch but far less in practice; 70% refuses both.

restarts.enforces: "A false start left in his take" (Krish, Tue 17): every restart is cut; one kept on purpose is listed in the spec (cuts.<id>.kept_restarts: [{at_s, why}]).

first_seconds.enforces: "considering that's the first few seconds of the video, it's not much of a hook. It looks quite dull for the first 3 seconds." (Krish, Wed 18): something moves from his first word.

head.enforces: "Can't cut my head off" and "my head needs to be in the bottom right" (Krish, Wed 18): on his lines his whole head is in frame, and on a 16:9 cut his take sits bottom right unless a full-frame clip fills the frame.
